newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom sees 800,000 mobile phone users end-1997.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom sees 800,000 mobile phone users end-1997.

text.p: Belgacom Mobile said on Friday it expected there to be 800,000 mobile phone users in Belgium by the end of 1997, around double the present number.
"For 1997 we can safely assume that eight percent of the entire Belgian population will own a GSM," the company said in a statement.
Belgacom Mobile, 75-percent owned by Belgian state telephone operator Belgacom and 25-percent by AirTouch Communications, is one of Belgium's two mobile phone companies.
The second operator Mobistar, which is majority owned by France Telecom FTE.PA launched at the end of August.

Belgacom Mobile chief executive officer Jan Neels said that despite the increased competition 1996 had been a very successful year, with GSM subscriptions up more than 100,000 to 370,000. Including its analogue mobile phone network, Belgacom Mobile's subscription base would exceed 400,000, he said.

"We will have achieved 4.5 percent market penetration by the end of the year," Neels said. "We expect the market to grow even Neels said that by 2000, two million Belgians, or one-in-five of the population, would probably have a mobile phone.
Mobistar, which had 60,000 GSM subscribers at the end of October, has said it hopes to have 11 percent of the Belgian market by 2000.

Erik Theyssens, telecommunications analyst at Banque Bruxelles Lambert, said earlier this week at a presentation of the bank's stock picks for 1997, that mobile phone operators had proved a cash cow for fixed network operators like Belgacom.
He estimated Belgacom Mobile was generating the group revenues in excess of 1.5 billion Belgian francs a month. "This is of course improving the bottom line," he said.
